content: Define a primary metric and a minimum detectable effect (MDE) in a JSON schema before starting any experiment. Failure to pre-define these leads to p-hacking and post-hoc rationalization of noise.

Use deterministic hashing of user IDs with a salt for traffic splitting to ensure consistent assignment across sessions. Store these assignments in a dedicated SQLite table with a unique constraint on user_id and experiment_id.

Log every exposure event to a dedicated event table including the variant, timestamp, and user context. Without an immutable exposure log, you cannot accurately calculate the denominator for conversion rates.

Calculate p-values using Welch's t-test or Mann-Whitney U test via scipy.stats to account for unequal variances between groups. Do not assume normal distribution for conversion data without validation.

Implement a kill-switch for every experiment that defaults to the control group (A) if the feature flag service or database query fails. System stability must always take precedence over data collection.

Verify prompt versioning by embedding a unique hash of the LLM prompt template in the metadata of every completion request. This ensures that metrics can be segmented by the exact prompt string used during the test.
Validate sample ratio mismatch (SRM) using a Chi-squared test at the start of every analysis. An SRM indicates a bug in the splitting logic or a logging bias that invalidates all results.

Exclude bot traffic and internal test accounts from statistical calculations using a boolean filter in your SQL queries. Including non-human behavior inflates variance and masks the true treatment effect.

When testing LLM prompts, use a fixed seed and temperature of zero for evaluation sets to reduce stochastic noise. High variance in model outputs requires significantly larger sample sizes to reach significance.

Pre-Registration Pattern: Create a Pydantic model defining the hypothesis, target audience, and success criteria, then store it as a static file in the repository. Use this to automate the generation of the final analysis report and prevent goalpost-shifting.

Sticky Assignment Pattern: Use a SQLite table with (user_id, experiment_id, variant) as a primary key to store the first-time assignment. Query this table using an 'INSERT OR IGNORE' statement to ensure users never switch groups mid-experiment.

Counter-Metric Pattern: Always track a 'guardrail' metric, such as latency or error rate, alongside your primary conversion metric. This pattern prevents the agent from optimizing for one metric while inadvertently degrading the overall system performance.

Sequential Analysis Pattern: Use the Wald Sequential Probability Ratio Test (SPRT) to monitor results in real-time without the risk of 'peeking'. This allows for stopping experiments early if a variant is performing exceptionally poorly or well.

Canary Deployment Pattern: Deploy the B variant to a 1% subset of traffic while monitoring for 5xx errors via httpx and stamina. If error rates exceed a predefined threshold, automatically trigger a rollback before expanding the rollout.

Prompt Shadow Testing Pattern: Run a new LLM prompt version in parallel with the production prompt but do not show the output to the user. Log both results and use an LLM-as-a-judge to compare them before committing to a real A/B test.

Layered Experiment Pattern: Use different salt values for different experiment layers to allow for overlapping tests without interference. This enables the agent to test UI changes and backend prompt changes simultaneously on the same user base.

Standardized Metric Registry Pattern: Define all business metrics as reusable SQL snippets or Python functions using Pydantic for validation. This ensures consistency across multiple experiments and prevents custom, error-prone calculations per test.

Bootstrap Confidence Interval Pattern: Use the bootstrap method to estimate confidence intervals for non-standard metrics like ratios or percentiles. This provides a more robust measure of uncertainty when data does not follow a standard parametric distribution.

Feature Flag Toggle Pattern: Implement a dictionary-based configuration loaded into the app state that controls experiment exposure. Use this pattern to enable or disable experiments instantly without requiring a full CI/CD deployment cycle.

NEVER: Change the experiment configuration while it is running — WHY: Modifying parameters like MDE or traffic split mid-test introduces selection bias — INSTEAD: Stop the current test, analyze it, and start a new 'Phase 2' experiment.

NEVER: Use random.random() for traffic splitting — WHY: Random splits are not idempotent and will cause users to see different variants on page refresh — INSTEAD: Use zlib.crc32 or hashlib.md5 on the user ID for deterministic bucket assignment.

NEVER: Optimize for vanity metrics like 'total clicks' — WHY: These metrics don't correlate with long-term value and are easily gamed — INSTEAD: Focus on retention, revenue, or successful LLM task completion rates.

NEVER: Stop an experiment the moment it reaches p < 0.05 — WHY: The 'peeking problem' leads to a high false-positive rate as results fluctuate — INSTEAD: Wait until the pre-calculated sample size is reached.

NEVER: Hardcode experiment logic directly into business logic functions — WHY: It creates 'technical debt' that is difficult to clean up after the test ends — INSTEAD: Use a middleware or a decorator to inject the variant choice.

NEVER: Test multiple unrelated changes in a single variant — WHY: You won't be able to isolate which change caused the impact — INSTEAD: Use a multivariate test or sequential A/B tests for each individual hypothesis.

NEVER: Ignore the cost of LLM tokens in prompt A/B testing — WHY: A 'better' prompt that is 10x more expensive might result in a negative ROI — INSTEAD: Include 'Cost per Successful Completion' as a secondary metric.

NEVER: Use a 50/50 split for a high-risk change — WHY: A bad variant could cause significant revenue loss or user churn — INSTEAD: Start with a 95/5 split and gradually increase the exposure as confidence grows.
MANDATORY: Use pytest (functions starting with test_) instead of unittest.TestCase. Always follow the specific linting and typing rules defined in pyproject.toml.

MANDATORY: __init__.py files MUST remain empty unless explicit exports are required. NEVER add unused imports like 'unittest' or chimerical modules to __init__.py. If a linter reports F401 in __init__.py, remove the line immediately.

CRITICAL ATOMICITY RULE: Every TASK in [AGENT_PROGRESS] MUST be a complete verifiable unit. NEVER create separate tasks for 'writing code' and 'writing tests'. The implementation of a feature and its corresponding unit tests MUST always be grouped into a single, atomic TASK to ensure verification integrity.

TRUTH RULE: When analyzing requirements, cross-reference every file and function name against the provided <codebase_map>. If a file or function is not in the map, treat it as non-existent. NEVER plan an update to a function that is not explicitly listed in the map; plan a creation instead.

VERIFICATION CONTRACT: Every TASK description in [AGENT_PROGRESS] must include an explicit success criterion. Instead of 'Implement X', use 'Implement X and verify it passes pytest with 100% coverage for the new logic'. This creates a binding contract for the Implementer and the Auditor.

COHESION RULE: Group logic by domain responsibility. If a new function does not logically extend an existing module's single responsibility, plan a new module. Avoid 'god-modules' like utils.py. If planning a new directory, always include the creation of an empty __init__.py file in the task.

TASK ECONOMY: For features under 50 lines of code, favor a single atomic TASK. Over-partitioning simple goals into multiple tasks increases token overhead and the risk of context drift. Minimize the number of tasks without sacrificing atomicity.

DEPENDENCY FIRST: Before planning any EXECUTING task, explicitly list all new external dependencies required. If a new import is needed that is not in pyproject.toml, create a separate TASK-000 to add it via 'uv add'. Never assume a library is available without verifying it in the codebase_map.

TEST-FIRST CONTRACT: Every EXECUTING task that creates or modifies a function must include a paired test task. The test task must be planned BEFORE the implementation task in [AGENT_PROGRESS]. Pattern: TASK-N: Write test for X, TASK-N+1: Implement X. Never plan implementation without a corresponding test.

ROLLBACK AWARENESS: If a TASK modifies an existing function (not creates new), add a comment with the original function signature as a inline backup. Format: '# ORIGINAL: def func(a: int) -> str'. This enables instant rollback without git history lookup.

NEVER: Mark a TASK as complete based solely on 'no errors in output'. ALWAYS require explicit PASS signal from testing-pro skill (RESULT:PASS). A silent execution without test output means the test suite did not run, not that it passed.

SCOPE BOUNDARY: A GOAL must produce changes in maximum 3 files. If the analysis shows more than 3 files need modification, decompose the GOAL into multiple smaller GOALs in [USER_QUEUE]. Large-scope changes increase context drift and reduce Auditor accuracy.

NEVER: Plan a rename or move of existing functions/files unless explicitly requested by the operator. Renaming breaks imports across the codebase and requires updating all callers. If a better name is identified, log it as a suggestion in SESSION.md [AGENT_SECTION] instead of acting on it.

FILE SIZE CEILING: No Python file in src/ should exceed 200 lines. Files in agent_core/ framework have a limit of 350 lines due to inherent complexity. Files in tests/ are exempt to allow for fixture chains. If a TASK involves a file approaching its limit, Queen MUST plan a refactoring TASK to split the module before adding new logic.

SIDE-EFFECT ISOLATION: Functional logic (pure) and I/O operations (file system, network, console) MUST be separated. Pure functions return data; wrapper functions handle I/O. Example: 'calculate_stats(data) -> Result' is a pure function; 'save_stats(path, result)' is its I/O wrapper. Queen must plan functions that return data instead of printing it to ensure easy mocking in tests.

REFACTORING ISOLATION: Never mix refactoring and new feature implementation in a single TASK. If existing code needs improvement to support a new goal, create a dedicated 'Refactor X' task first, followed by 'Implement Y'. This ensures a clean git history and prevents cascading linter failures.

LIBRARY MINIMALISM: Avoid external dependencies for tasks solvable via the Python Standard Library. Approved lightweight libs: httpx, stamina, pydantic, structlog, typer. Heavy frameworks requiring explicit justification: pandas, numpy, sqlalchemy, django. If a new library is proposed, Queen must justify it in the <thinking> section based on ROI.

DOC-SYNC & STANDARDS: When a TASK modifies the behavior or signature of a function, the docstring MUST be updated in the same TASK. All docstrings MUST follow Google-style (including Args, Returns, and Raises sections). Functions under 5 lines of code may use a concise single-line docstring. Consistent documentation is critical for RAG system accuracy.
NO-PASS POLICY: Never use 'pass' in function skeletons if a return type is defined. Always return a dummy value (e.g., return '', 0.0, or False) to satisfy Mypy immediately during EXECUTING.

MOCKING STANDARD: All external I/O (APIs, Database, File System) MUST be mocked in tests. Tests must be executable offline and produce deterministic results. Never assume external services are available.
SECURITY GUARDRAIL: Hardcoded credentials or API keys are strictly forbidden. Discovery of such patterns during VERIFYING result in immediate REJECT. Use environment variables via load_env().
NEVER: Use 'print()' in production code (src/). INSTEAD: Use structured logging via 'log' utility or 'structlog'. Prints are allowed ONLY in tests/ for debugging.

SILENT SUCCESS TRAP: NEVER mark a task as complete based on 'no errors in output'. ALWAYS require explicit 'RESULT:PASS' from testing-pro. Silent execution means tests did not run, not that they passed.
COMMIT INTEGRITY: All automated commits must follow Conventional Commits. Format: 'feat(scope): desc' or 'fix(scope): desc'. Auditor must reject vague or non-standard commit messages.

TYPE NARROWING: Never use 'Any' as a type hint except in adapter/bridge code. If the type is truly unknown, use 'object' or define a Union. Every 'Any' in src/ is a Mypy debt that will surface as a runtime bug.

EXCEPTION SPECIFICITY: Never catch bare 'except:' or 'except Exception:' without re-raising or logging. Always catch the most specific exception type. Pattern: except httpx.TimeoutException as e: log.warning('timeout', error=str(e)).

EARLY RETURN PATTERN: Prefer early returns over nested if-else blocks. Validate preconditions at the top of the function and return/raise immediately. This reduces cognitive complexity and satisfies Ruff complexity rules automatically.

CONSTANT EXTRACTION: Magic numbers and hardcoded strings MUST be extracted to module-level constants with SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE names. Never use raw literals like 0.7, 90, 'local' directly in logic — these are invisible bugs waiting to happen.

ASYNC BOUNDARY: Never mix sync and async code in the same function. If a function calls 'await', its entire call chain must be async. Never call asyncio.run() inside an already running event loop — use httpx.AsyncClient only in async contexts.

RESOURCE CLEANUP: All resources that require explicit closing (files, DB connections, HTTP clients) MUST be managed via context managers ('with' or 'async with'). Never rely on garbage collection for cleanup — especially critical for SQLite WAL connections.

PYDANTIC OVER DICT PATTERN: Never pass raw dicts between functions when the structure is known. Define a Pydantic model instead. This catches schema mismatches at the boundary, not deep in the call stack where debugging is expensive.

TEST NAMING: Test functions must follow pattern 'test_[unit]_[scenario]_[expected]'. Example: 'test_login_invalid_password_returns_401'. A test name must be a complete sentence describing what is verified — never use 'test_1' or 'test_login'.

PARAMETRIZE PATTERN: When testing the same logic with multiple inputs or edge cases, use @pytest.mark.parametrize. Even TWO test cases (happy path + edge case) should use parametrize instead of separate assert statements. This enforces DRY principle.

FIXTURE SCOPE: Use 'scope=session' for expensive fixtures (DB init, HTTP client), 'scope=function' for mutable state. A slow test suite is almost always caused by session-level setup running at function scope. Always declare scope explicitly — never rely on the default.

COVERAGE THRESHOLD: Minimum 80% test coverage is required for every new module in src/. Auditor must reject any TASK marked complete where coverage-pro reports below this threshold. Use 'pytest --cov=src --cov-fail-under=80' as the verification command.

RUFF ZERO TOLERANCE: Zero Ruff violations are required before LINTING stage can pass. Pedant must run 'ruff check src/' and 'ruff format --check src/' as separate commands. A single violation blocks the pipeline — no exceptions, no inline suppressions without justification comment.

MYPY STRICT BOUNDARY: All new code in src/ must pass 'mypy src/ --disallow-untyped-defs'. Mypy errors are Developer responsibility, not Pedant. Pedant reports Mypy failures but Developer must fix them in a new EXECUTING attempt.

NOQA JUSTIFICATION: Every '# noqa' inline suppression MUST be accompanied by a comment explaining why the rule is suppressed. Format: '# noqa: E501 — URL cannot be shortened'. Unjustified suppressions are treated as violations by Pedant.

NEVER: Leave unused imports in src/ files. Ruff rule F401 catches these automatically. Dead imports increase cognitive load, slow down module initialization and signal incomplete refactoring. Pedant must treat F401 violations as blockers.

COMPLEXITY CEILING: Maximum cyclomatic complexity per function is 10 (Ruff rule C901). If Pedant detects a function exceeding this limit, it must request Developer to refactor using Early Return Pattern or extract helper functions before proceeding.

ASSERTION QUALITY: Every test must contain at least one meaningful assertion. Tests with only 'assert True' or no assertion are treated as phantom tests — they provide false coverage without verification. Auditor must check assertion density in coverage report.

REGRESSION GUARD: Before marking a GOAL complete, Auditor must verify that ALL existing tests still pass — not just the new ones. A feature that breaks existing tests is a regression, not progress. Run full 'pytest tests/' not just the new test file.

SECURITY SCAN SEQUENCE: Auditor must execute security-guard skill BEFORE reviewing test results. If security-guard returns HALT, the pipeline stops immediately regardless of test status. Security violations outrank all other quality metrics.

DOCSTRING COVERAGE: Every public function and class in src/ must have a Google-style docstring with at minimum a one-line summary. Missing docstrings degrade RAG accuracy in codebase_nodes and signal incomplete implementation. Pedant treats missing docstrings as warnings, not blockers.

TEST ISOLATION: Tests must not depend on execution order. Requires 'pytest-randomly' in dev-dependencies (pyproject.toml). Auditor must verify by running 'pytest --randomly-seed=last tests/' after standard run. If results differ, Developer must fix shared state in fixtures before GOAL can be closed.

NEVER: Use deprecated Python patterns flagged by Ruff UP (pyupgrade) rules. Examples: 'typing.List' instead of 'list', 'typing.Optional' instead of 'X | None', 'os.path' instead of 'pathlib.Path'. Pedant must treat UP violations as blockers in Python 3.12 codebase.

BRANCH NAMING: Every automated branch must follow pattern 'type/GOAL-XXX-short-description'. Types: feat, fix, refactor, test, docs. Example: 'feat/GOAL-001-add-greet-function'. Git-Mgr must reject branch creation that does not match this pattern.

ATOMIC COMMITS: One commit = one logical change. Never bundle multiple TASK completions into a single commit. Git-Mgr must create one commit per completed TASK, not one commit per GOAL. This enables precise git bisect and rollback.

PR DESCRIPTION CONTRACT: Every automated PR must include three sections: '## What changed' (list of modified files), '## Why' (GOAL description from TASKS.md), '## Verification' (pytest output summary and coverage percentage). PRs without these sections must be rejected by Auditor.

NEVER: Use 'git push --force' on any branch. REASON: Force push rewrites history and destroys audit trail in execution_logs. INSTEAD: Use 'git push --force-with-lease' only when explicitly requested by operator, never autonomously.

RELEASE TAGGING: When a GOAL closes a milestone (detected by keyword 'milestone' in GOAL description), Git-Mgr must create a semantic version tag. Format: 'vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH'. Tag message must reference the GOAL-XXX identifier for traceability.

CLEAN TREE CHECK: Git-Mgr must verify 'git status --porcelain' returns empty before creating a commit. If untracked or modified files exist outside the planned TASK scope, Git-Mgr must HALT and report to operator. Never commit files that were not part of the TASK plan.

NEVER: Commit .env files or files containing API keys to git history. REASON: git history is permanent — even after deletion the secret remains in history. INSTEAD: Verify '.env' is in .gitignore before every commit. If secret is accidentally committed, treat as HALT and rotate the key immediately.

GHA STATUS GATE: In CI_MODE=github, Auditor must wait for all GitHub Actions checks to pass before approving PR merge. If 'watch_gha=true' and GHA fails, Auditor must pull the failure logs and inject them into SESSION.md as a new EXECUTING task. Never merge a PR with failing checks.

MERGE STRATEGY: All PRs must use 'Squash and Merge' for feature branches and 'Merge Commit' for release branches. Squash keeps main branch history linear and readable. Git-Mgr must set merge strategy based on branch type prefix: feat/fix/refactor = squash, release = merge commit.

ROLLBACK PROTOCOL: If VERIFYING fails after VCS_DELIVERY has already pushed a branch, Git-Mgr must not delete the branch. Instead: create a revert commit, push it, and update TASKS.md with BLOCKED status. Preserve all evidence for debugging — never silently clean up failed deliveries.

CHANGELOG UPDATE: Every merged GOAL must append an entry to CHANGELOG.md before the final commit. Format: '## [GOAL-XXX] - YYYY-MM-DD: short description'. Git-Mgr is responsible for this step. A missing CHANGELOG entry is treated as incomplete delivery.
NEVER: Add unrecognized flags to pytest addopts in pyproject.toml. REASON: Invalid addopts flags cause pytest to refuse

AUDITOR FEEDBACK PRECISION: When VERIFYING fails, Auditor MUST specify: (1) which check failed (ruff/mypy/pytest/security), (2) the exact error message, (3) which file caused the failure. 'Quality gate failed' without specifics is not actionable and wastes a retry attempt.

NEVER: Import or use the 'unittest' module. REASON: Our framework runs strictly on 'pytest'. Using 'unittest.TestCase' classes creates boilerplate and breaks modern fixture isolation. INSTEAD: Write pure test functions starting with 'test_'. If you need setup/teardown, use @pytest.fixture.

NEVER: Import 'os' or use 'os.path' for file system operations. REASON: It is legacy Python. INSTEAD: Always use 'from pathlib import Path' and its object-oriented methods (e.g., Path(file).exists(), Path(file).read_text()).

TEST MIRRORING RULE: The name of the test file MUST exactly match the name of the source module, prefixed with 'test_'. Example: If implementing in 'src/greeting.py', the test MUST be in 'tests/test_greeting.py'. Never mix module names across src/ and tests/.

YAGNI RULE (You Aren't Gonna Need It): Implement ONLY the function explicitly requested in the task description. NEVER add extra utility functions, helper methods, or classes unless strictly necessary to pass the test. Keep the codebase minimal.

NEVER: Decompose a feature into separate tasks for 'code' and 'tests'. REASON: This breaks the TDD verification loop and causes cascading failures in LINTING and VERIFYING stages. INSTEAD: ALWAYS plan a single, atomic task that includes implementation, testing, and verification in its description.

NEVER: Use <file_write> tags to modify agent_context/SESSION.md or agent_context/TASKS.md. REASON: The Router engine manages system state automatically based on your task completion. Attempting to overwrite session files will trigger the Bimetric Shield security block. INSTEAD: Only write to src/ and tests/ directories.

JSON BREVITY RULE: When populating the 'description' field in the AtomicTask JSON response, be extremely concise (max 3-4 sentences). NEVER use large markdown lists, TDD tutorials, or step-by-step guides inside the JSON string. The Developer already knows HOW to code; just tell them WHAT to code.

PYTEST PARAMETRIZE MANDATE: NEVER write multiple sequential 'assert' statements in a single test function to verify different inputs for the same logic. INSTEAD: You MUST use '@pytest.mark.parametrize' to feed multiple test cases (happy path, edge cases) into a single, clean test function. This enforces the DRY principle and makes test failures easier to debug.

EXCEPTION SEMANTICS RULE (TRY004): To satisfy the linter, you must use the correct exception type. Use 'TypeError' when checking if an object is of the wrong type (e.g., isinstance(product, Product)). Use 'ValueError' when the object has the right type, but its value is invalid (e.g., price = -10).

ANTI-MICROMANAGEMENT RULE: NEVER decompose the implementation of a single, cohesive class into multiple sequential tasks (one for each method). REASON: This wastes tokens and time, and creates linter/type conflicts between steps. INSTEAD: The entire implementation of a class and all its tests MUST be planned in ONE SINGLE AtomicTask. Violation will be treated as a planning failure.

GOAL SPECIFICATION PROTOCOL: Every GOAL in [USER_QUEUE] must contain three sections: INTENT (what and why), CONSTRAINTS (boundaries the agent must not cross), METRIC (machine-readable thresholds e.g. coverage>=80 complexity<=5 mypy=strict noqa=0). Goals without all three sections are rejected by Queen in STRATEGY stage without calling LLM.

NEVER: Place 'import' statements inside test functions (inline imports). REASON: Inline imports hide dependencies, reduce readability, and cause F821 undefined name errors if the linter is misconfigured. INSTEAD: All imports MUST be declared at the top of the file, immediately after the module docstring.

TESTING MANDATE: Every logic implementation requires at least TWO test cases (Happy Path and Edge Case like None/empty). To adhere to the DRY principle, Queen MUST explicitly instruct the Developer to use '@pytest.mark.parametrize' for these cases instead of writing separate test functions.

NEVER: Omit the METRIC string from a TASK description. REASON: If the GOAL contains a METRIC threshold (e.g., coverage>=90), the Developer and Auditor will not know the pass/fail criteria unless it is explicitly written in the TASK. INSTEAD: You MUST copy the exact METRIC string from the GOAL and append it to the 'description' field of EVERY task you generate.

CONTEXT MANAGER CONTRACT: The '__exit__' method MUST follow this strict signature: 'def __exit__(self, exc_type: type[BaseException] | None, exc_val: BaseException | None, exc_tb: types.TracebackType | None) -> None:'. You MUST import 'TracebackType' from 'types'. Never use 'Any' for these arguments.
PATHLIB OPEN: Favor 'Path.open()' over the global 'open()' function. Example: 'with self.file_path.open(mode) as f:'. This satisfies both Pathlib standards and simplifies context management.

RESOURCE SUPPRESSION: When a class is designed to manage a long-lived file handle (opened in __init__ and closed in __exit__), use '# noqa: SIM115' on the open call. This explicitly signals that the resource leak is prevented by the class's own context manager logic.

TOP-LEVEL IMPORTS: All imports in test files MUST be at the top of the file, immediately after the module docstring. Never place imports inside test functions. Correct: 'from src.module import function' at top of file. This applies to ALL test files without exception.

IMPORT HYGIENE: Every import statement must be used. Never add 'import pytest' unless you explicitly use pytest fixtures, marks, or raises. Unused imports cause Ruff F401 violation. If you use @pytest.mark.parametrize, import pytest. If you only use assert, do NOT import pytest.

MODULE DOCSTRING: Every Python file in src/ and tests/ MUST start with a module-level docstring immediately after any future imports. Format: triple-quoted string with module description. Missing module docstring causes mypy and ruff warnings.

EXCEPTION RAISING MANDATE: NEVER use 'assert' statements in 'src/' for data validation. 'assert' is only for 'tests/'. INSTEAD: Explicitly raise specific exceptions like 'ValueError' (for invalid data like division by zero) or 'TypeError' (for invalid types) with descriptive error messages.

TYPE CHECKING PATTERN: When manually validating numeric inputs without Pydantic, ALWAYS use 'isinstance(value, (int, float))' and explicitly exclude boolean (since bool is a subclass of int in Python) using 'not isinstance(value, bool)'. NEVER use 'type(value) == int'.

PYDANTIC V2 VALIDATORS: Use @field_validator not @validator (V1 syntax). For model-level validation use @model_validator(mode='before'). Never use class Config, use model_config = ConfigDict() instead.

TYPE ANNOTATIONS MANDATE: Every method, classmethod and staticmethod MUST have explicit return type annotation. __init__ returns None, classmethods return their type. Examples: 'def __init__(self) -> None', '@classmethod def create(cls, v: float) -> float'. Missing annotations cause Ruff ANN201/ANN204/ANN206 errors.
